Six runtime plugins install separately from authorized declared origins in fixed order while contracts remain non-runtime.
Canvas lists selects and switches local Luanti world connections and binds through the Adapter handshake with a version-matched payload and stable world identity.
Canvas binds operator-authorized remote Luanti and missing payload or permission reports the exact prerequisite with zero mutation.
One Session switches local and remote worlds without splitting and ambiguous cross-world references require clarification.
Shell and Luanti resume the same Session turn and revision after restart.
The supported host model attachment path sends user-provided text and image together to gpt-5.6-luna without embedding image bytes in text subprocess arguments logs or uncontrolled requests.
When the image or combined image-text intent is unclear Workshop continues the same Session and asks for supplemental text instead of guessing.
Shell controls complete Building Exterior creation from required user image plus text, place/readback, name/select/rename the object.
Luanti in-world controls complete Building Exterior creation from required user image plus text, place/readback, name/select/rename the object.
Shell controls complete Building Interior modification from selected real occupancy/cavity plus text and optional style image.
Luanti in-world controls complete Building Interior modification from selected real occupancy/cavity plus text and optional style image.

Canvas lists creates names renames and inspects objects and atomically replaces the ordered zero-or-more object selection including empty clear; registry selection and rename persist across Shell DSH and Luanti restart.

Normal single-object work has no preview; complete durable before-image precedes recoverable apply, complete readback and linked-history barrier precede success. Construction may be visible; no strict engine invisibility promise.

Other-object impact blocks before mutation; explicit same-plan continuation applies one linked recoverable multi-object operation with one history entry; complete readback and all linked heads precede success.

Apply/readback failure attempts complete scoped restoration; verified restoration reports ROLLED_BACK. Failed/unknown recovery retains scene/journal, reports RESTORE_FAILED/RECOVERY_PENDING/UNKNOWN honestly and prevents new same-scope mutation, never partial success.

Per-object and linked multi-object undo/redo persist across restart, compare actual expected state and read back recoverable whole linked operation before all history heads advance. Later player edits cause zero-write Session proposal and preserve heads pending new confirmed authority.
A new edit after undo abandons the redo branch and that state survives restart.
Every repository clean clone build package and install succeeds without developer paths local archives file or link dependencies caches or live profile state.
Restart uninstall and reinstall and rollback restore the recorded composition with no undeclared residue.
Source revision version lock artifact manifest install receipt installed bytes and loaded bytes agree.
Local integration completes the entire Stage 1 matrix independently through Shell controls only and Luanti in-world controls only with the same transaction and readback semantics.
Connection model media object history payload identity and invariant projections are visible and correctly attributed in Shell management UI.
After engineering integration is green the authorized user independently completes Human Manual Validation and alone records ACCEPTED.
All seven exact v2 ports, nineteen digest projections, strict admission and all canonical valid/invalid closure oracles pass; no provider implementation or private reduced schema.

Crash before write, mid-write, after apply/before readback and after VERIFIED resolves to one truthful durable receipt; missing restoration retains scene/journal and prevents new same-scope write; later edits trigger proposal, never blind undo.

True Session delete uses supported public host seam and does not delete current placed buildings/history/required payload resources; archive is not delete. Fixed Core lacks seam, so this gate must remain open until explicitly authorized provider closure.

A first new building requested in Luanti goes on free ground in front of the initiating player along the facing direction with its entrance toward the player; from Shell with exactly one online player it goes in front of that player; the placement.* settings (defaults 2/16/8/4) are honored; no fictitious object or initial PLANNED state is used.

With several online players for a Shell-started turn, the plugin lists their names (names only, shown only to a user authorized for the bound world) for the user to tap one, or to pick an in-game point; with no online player, an offline initiator, an ambiguous facing, or an unusable front area (occupied, protected, a player body, no ground, unknown), it states why and asks the user to pick an in-game point. It never guesses a player or silently relocates, performs zero world writes before the choice, and Prepare rechecks protection and player bodies.

The four placement settings and the rc.6 placement invariants are visible in the Shell management interface with owner, default and on/off consequence; the settings are editable there, invariants are shown as not switchable, and an unset or invalid setting yields a typed CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE naming it.

A first new building requested in Luanti goes on free ground in front of the initiating player along the facing direction with its entrance toward the player; from Shell with exactly one online player it goes in front of that player; the placement.* settings (defaults 2/16/8/4) are honored; no fictitious object or initial PLANNED state is used.

With several online players for a Shell-started turn, the plugin lists their names (names only, shown only to a user authorized for the bound world) for the user to tap one, or to pick an in-game point; with no online player, an offline initiator, an ambiguous facing, or an unusable front area (occupied, protected, a player body, no ground, unknown), it states why and asks the user to pick an in-game point. It never guesses a player or silently relocates, performs zero world writes before the choice, and Prepare rechecks protection and player bodies.

The four placement settings and the rc.6 placement invariants are visible in the Shell management interface with owner, default and on/off consequence; the settings are editable there, invariants are shown as not switchable, and an unset or invalid setting yields a typed CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE naming it.
